runs.name: The Southern Company; NYSE SO, SEC CIK 0000092122; utility holding company: Alabama Power, Georgia Power and Mississippi Power, vertically integrated utilities in three Southeastern states, Southern Power selling at market-based rates in the wholesale market, Southern Company Gas distributing gas in Illinois, Georgia, Virginia and Tennessee; three reportable segments; no rename, merger, spin-off or split seen in the recent 8-Ks; convertible senior notes of $833.75M and $1,897.5M issued 2026-08-06, an equity distribution agreement of 2026-06-08
runs.box: OUT AT Q7, ON THE FLOOR
runs.entry: The v5 re-run order, unattended work-hours cycle, one dispatched analyst under the canonical brief, a RESUME: the 11:30 cycle was stopped by a usage limit after the template was copied (title line only, nothing committed) and the 12:00 and 12:30 cycles were rate limited; the 13:00 cycle dispatched the resume. The brief's departures: the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25, the lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, the rivals taken from the 10-K, the resume paragraph, and a line pointing to Q7, The regulated utility, with Southern Power named as the merchant part. Price **$92.69** (2026-10-26, aggregator, flagged; the run calls it a close, taken intraday) x **1,150,362,966 shares** (10-Q cover at 2026-06-30, accession 0000092122-26-000054; forward sales, equity units and convertibles not counted, stated at Q6) = cap **$106,627M**; sovereign **5.33%** (Treasury 30-year par, 2026-10-23). Read from the 10-K for 2025 (0000092122-26-000006), the 10-Ks for 2023 and 2017, two 10-Qs, the 2026 proxy and the 8-Ks. **Q1 IN** (the three electric utilities decide, 79% of 2021 to 2025 segment net income; gas 14%, Southern Power 6%). **Q2 IN** (statutory territories and exclusive gas franchises; the regulator-set return carried to Q3 as a second best by the framework's text; the owners bore the Kemper and Vogtle overruns). **Q3 UNDECIDED** (about 6.7% on added tangible capital; owner cash negative after all spending every year). **Q4 WEIGHS AGAINST** (ten balance sheets 2016 to 2025: debt $47.5B to $72.6B, common equity up 45%, shares up about 16%, retained earnings cut by the 2017 Kemper charges; recurring charges, about $3.8B pre-tax Kemper 2016 to 2017 and about $2.9B Vogtle 2018 to 2022). **Q5 integrity IN** (the SEC Kemper investigation closed November 2017 with no enforcement recommended; the securities class action settled for $87.5M by insurers, liability denied; the opposing reading written down), **ability WEIGHS AGAINST**. **Q6 WEIGHS AGAINST** (the dividend of about $3.0B funded by debt and continuous issuance, about $2.5B of stock in the first half of 2026; CEO pay $28.2M on adjusted EPS against guidance, relative return and ROE). **Q7 OUT on the floor**: owner cash 2021 to 2025 about -$2.3B a year after all spending, $2,797M equity-only maintenance only (depreciation the guess, cross-checked against the filing's maintaining categories); growth 11.77% a year for ten years, under the (f) cap (15.57% against 15.73%); debt credit $2,188M a year against growth spending only, long-term debt up $4,658M a year, capped at Georgia Power's 44% allowed debt share weighted by net plant (CONVENTION of the run, rate base not stated by company); equity-only range **$45.62 to $82.70 a share** (central, a regulated utility), the cases return 2.62% and about 4.94% at the price; own-share cap beside, top $96.44, box unchanged; fair price **$26.47 equity-only**, all-equity -$22.61, not positive. Southern Power valued inside the consolidated equity-only figure (CONVENTION of the run, cash flows not reported by segment). Q8 to Q12 not reached. Peers (the 10-K names no rival; Duke, Entergy, Dominion chosen as a CONVENTION of the run): return on average common equity Southern 12.0% (2021 to 2025), Duke 6.8%, Entergy 10.8% (2021 to 2024), Dominion 6.9% (2023 to 2024), missing years untagged. Facts after the stop: collateral of $3,774M on a fall to BB+ or below; pre-tax interest cover about 2.5 times in 2025. Framework gaps for the operator: the debt-credit cap when one company of a several-company deciding part states an allowed share and no rate base is stated by company; a consolidated utility holding company with a merchant part reported only in consolidated cash flows; which filed capital categories count as maintaining for a utility; the template's Q2 line omits the regulated-return exception the framework's Q2 contains; `Screens/cover_shares.py` labels the subsidiary registrants' common shares as note series; `tools/run.py`'s stock-pay column took an APIC tag giving about half the filed expense. Could not get: rate base by company, the rivals' missing years, Southern Power's own cash flows; the proxy read by search. Departure by the analyst: commits grouped (Step 0 to Q2, Q3 with Q4, Q5 with Q6, Q7 and the close), five pathspec commits of its own paths, last `06cbfc85`. Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; 74 ids resolve, no E-ids, no citation slip, 48 adjacent fragment pairs checked, two checker mispairings resolved by hand (the fragments belong to M2000-037 and L2000-035, beside which they stand) (`dispatcher_cite_check.py`); no tracked research file over 200 KB. Contamination declared: session-start git status and commit subjects of another company's run and fold, a research folder name, a memory index line naming no company; none used. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Armed at the equity-only fair price.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 on the floor: statutory franchises in three Southeastern states that earn their allowed returns, but owner cash is negative after all spending every year and the dividend is funded by debt and new stock; equity-only range $45.62 to $82.70 vs $92.69; fair $26.47 equity-only; no case earns the floor.
